extracted.intended_audience: energy regulators, NERC/FERC staff, utility compliance officers, energy lawyers, and stakeholders involved in reliability standards development and enforcement
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and applying criteria to assess the development, processing, and enforcement of mandatory electric reliability standards by the ERO (NERC), Regional Entities, and FERC, including procedural, documentation, and risk-based practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards content focus (Order No. 896 themes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability standards should address data sharing, model validation, planning and operational studies, and performance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC’s directives in the transmission-planning rule focused on these four high-level concerns and included many specific directives (the final rule contained more than sixty directives about expected content for new or modified standards). Use these topic areas as core dimensions when evaluating whether standards are responsive to Order No. 896.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and deadline compliance (Order No. 901 tranches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards development must meet FERC-directed scheduling (three-stage tranches and target implementation timeline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order No. 901 required NERC to submit standards in tranches (2024, 2025, 2026) and expressed a strong expectation to have directed reliability standards effective well in advance of 2030. NERC may use alternative procedures (Board authority) to meet FERC deadlines; timeliness is a substantive expectation from FERC that influences acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing articulated technical reliability gaps (e.g., inverter-based resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must directly address the specific reliability concern FERC identifies (for example, inverter-based resource performance and ride-through requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC has directed NERC to develop standards to close identified gaps and expects proposed standards to meaningfully address the articulated reliability issue; FERC states it is not dictating precise content but drives the problem definition and acceptable solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards development should begin from a common understanding achieved through formal or informal collaboration among FERC, NERC, industry stakeholders, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical conferences and stakeholder outreach improve goal definition and drafting direction, increase timeliness and efficiency, and raise the likelihood of FERC approval without corrective directives. Lack of common understanding is an anti-pattern that has led to breakdowns and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in standards-development procedures with preserved stakeholder participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Process rules may permit expedited or alternative procedures (e.g., Board direction in extraordinary circumstances; retiring ANSI requirement) provided stakeholder participation remains meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC revised rules to allow Board-directed development when stakeholder process fails and to retire mandatory ANSI certification to enable alternative but still-participatory processes. FERC accepts such flexibility but emphasizes continued timely and responsive standards development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-pillared enforcement framework
rubrics_metrics.description: A meaningful compliance and enforcement program requires: (1) a penalty program, (2) a compliance program including proactive audits, and (3) prompt notification to FERC of possible violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framework balances deterrence, prevention, and oversight. Each pillar must be implemented coherently — e.g., penalty guidelines and ranges, audit regimes, and prompt reporting procedures — to satisfy statutory responsibilities under section 215.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core oversight requirements: transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement program must be transparent: prompt notification of violations, maintenance of complete violation records, and preservation of review rights by FERC and the ERO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is required except where public dissemination would jeopardize system security. Public posting and accessible records support accountability and stakeholder confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core oversight requirements: verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERO must retain oversight responsibility, require Regional Entities to report periodically, and audit Regional Entity enforcement and compliance activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC must audit each Regional Entity’s ongoing compliance with statutory/regulatory criteria and report audit results to FERC. Verification ensures delegated authority is exercised properly and consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core oversight requirements: consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes, documentation, and sanction application should be uniform across Regional Entities unless justified by regional facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformity promotes fairness; delegation agreements should list statutory functions the Regional Entity performs, and the ERO must ensure consistent implementation. Regional variation is only acceptable for compelling, documented reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty proportionality and factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties must bear a reasonable relation to the seriousness of the violation and consider the violator’s timely remediation efforts; FERC historically applied an upper limit ($1,000,000/day/violation, adjusted by inflation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC must develop penalty guidelines identifying ranges of monetary and non-monetary penalties. When assessing penalties, documentation should tie specific facts of the violation to penalty factors (seriousness, risk, mitigation efforts, consistency, and effect on reliability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Penalty (NOP) documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NOPs must include the violator’s identity, the reliability standard/requirement violated, findings of fact, description of the penalty, and the record of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC expects sufficient detail on the duration (entire violation period in days), nature (facts supporting that a violation occurred), mitigation actions taken, verification of mitigation completion, and explanation linking facts to penalty factors. Completeness supports FERC’s ability to determine whether further review is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionality of record/detail to violation significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the submitted record should be proportional to the complexity and relative importance of the violations addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC permits abbreviated/streamlined NOP formats for violations that do not pose significant risk (e.g., 'parking ticket' analogy). However, documentation must still be reasonably auditable and sufficient to establish compliance and penalty rationale. Over-documentation for minimal-risk matters creates backlogs; under-documentation risks FERC review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-based processing and classification (violation risk factors and severity levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use violation risk factors and severity levels to classify violations and determine processing path (e.g., FFT, abbreviated NOP, administrative citation, full NOP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC assigns each Reliability Standard a violation risk factor and uses severity levels to calculate penalties. Risk-based approaches (Omnibus filings, FFT Find-Fix-Track-Report, abbreviated formats) are encouraged to focus resources on higher-impact issues while allowing expedited processing of minimal-risk violations. Formats limited to lower/medium risk may be phased or adjusted based on experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find-Fix-Track-Report (FFT) and expedited processing for minimal risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal-risk violations that have been mitigated/remedied may be processed via FFT with streamlined documentation and expedited resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FFT is intended to reduce paperwork and speed resolution for minimal-risk matters. NERC’s program included informational filings of FFT spreadsheets for possible violations posing minimal risk; the transparency and auditable nature of the FFT record remains important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for settlements and de novo review
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC will review settlement-based NOPs substantively (not categorically) and may conduct de novo review to assess whether the record supports that the penalty reasonably relates to seriousness and remediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat settlements like contested proceedings for documentation purposes: include adequate facts, mitigation verification, and penalty rationale to withstand independent Commission review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit program design: single, uniform program unless justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit programs should be a single program applicable to both the ERO and Regional Entities and should not vary significantly region-to-region absent good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC expects rigorous audits as a crucial element of ensuring reliability. Uniform audit programs promote fairness and aid verification by the ERO and FERC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of compliance staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance and enforcement staff of the ERO and Regional Entities must operate independently from undue industry influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence supports integrity of findings, audits, and enforcement decisions; delegation agreements and rules should preserve this independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive measures to reduce compliance risk and streamline consensus (e.g., abeyance periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural tools (such as compliance abeyance periods) may be used to minimize compliance risk concerns that stall consensus-building in standards development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC proposed abeyance periods after implementation of select standards to reduce perceived compliance risk and streamline stakeholder consensus processes; such measures should be evaluated for their effect on timely, effective standards adoption and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional filing formats and administrative citation limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamlined filing formats (abbreviated NOPs, administrative citations, SNOP spreadsheets) are acceptable for lower-risk matters but have scope limits and must still supply sufficient information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative citation formats can improve efficiency but may be constrained by risk-factor thresholds and may be modified or dropped if impractical. FERC expects appropriate detail to determine whether further review is necessary even for streamlined filings.
